{"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_anthropic-claude-haiku-5-5_01.html","edit_description":"Replace the ENTIRE file content with a complete, self-contained HTML5 document (no external libraries, no WebGL, Canvas 2D only). Title: "Gouraud Shaded Rotating Cube". Include inline CSS: dark background (#0b0d12), body centered, canvas fills viewport (or fixed 800x600 scaled to fit), and a small HUD overlay (top-left) showing "FPS: N" plus key help text "W: wireframe | P: pause | drag nothing". Use a <canvas id="c"> and a small <div id="hud">.

JavaScript requirements (all inline in one <script>):

1. Math: a tiny Vec3 helper set (functions on plain arrays [x,y,z]): add, sub, scale, dot, cross, normalize. Rotation matrices: rotX(a), rotY(a), rotZ(a) returning 3x3 arrays, and mulMatVec(m, v). Compose rotation = rotY * rotX * rotZ applied to each vertex each frame.

2. Geometry: a cube of half-size 1 with 6 faces. Each face has 4 UNIQUE vertices (24 total) so each face gets its own flat face normal and its own color; define faces as quads with CCW winding when viewed from outside, with an outward normal per face. Split each quad into two triangles: (0,1,2) and (0,2,3). Face colors: distinct hues (e.g. [230,80,80],[80,200,110],[80,130,240],[230,200,70],[200,90,220],[70,210,210]).

3. Per frame transform pipeline:
   - Rotate each vertex and each face normal with the rotation matrix (world space).
   - Camera at z distance D=5 looking down -z; view-space z = worldZ + D (or equivalent translation). Perspective projection: sx = cx + f * x / z, sy = cy - f * y / z, with f = min(width,height)*0.45 and z clamped to > 0.1. Keep per-vertex view-space (x,y,z) for lighting.
   - Backface culling: for each triangle compute the face normal in view space (cross of edges of the triangle in view space); cull if dot(normal, -viewPos_of_triangle_centroid) <= 0 (i.e. facing away from camera at origin). Simpler acceptable: use the projected 2D signed area; cull if signed area <= 0 depending on consistent winding. Make sure the visible faces are the ones drawn.
   - Lighting per VERTEX (Lambert + ambient): light position moves in a circle/ellipse around the cube in world space, e.g. L(t) = [3*cos(t), 2.2*sin(0.7t), 3*sin(t)] with t advancing by dt when not paused. Per vertex: N = rotated face normal (world space), Ldir = normalize(lightPos - vertexWorldPos), diff = max(0, dot(N, Ldir)), with mild distance attenuation; intensity = clamp(ambient 0.15 + 0.85*diff, 0, 1). Vertex color = faceColor * intensity (store r,g,b per vertex).
   - Also draw a small visible light marker: project the light position and draw a bright glowing dot with canvas radial gradient in the 2D overlay.

4. Rasterization (Gouraud): create an ImageData of the canvas size (or use a backing buffer at device-pixel resolution); a Uint32Array view. Clear to background each frame. For each visible triangle with projected 2D vertices (x,y) and per-vertex colors (r,g,b): compute bounding box clipped to the screen; for every pixel center in the box compute barycentric weights w0,w1,w2 via edge functions (divide by total area); if all >= 0 (inside), interpolate r,g,b with the barycentric weights (this is the Gouraud color interpolation) and write the pixel. Use integer-safe math, precompute per-triangle edge coefficients for speed. Then putImageData once per frame. Do not write fill-style polygons for the faces — use the software rasterizer.

5. Wireframe mode (toggle with key W): when enabled, skip the pixel-fill step and instead stroke each visible triangle's three edges with ctx.strokeStyle '#e8f0ff' lineWidth 1 over the background; optionally still show filled faces dimmed — keep it simple: wireframe = edges only.

6. Pause (key P): toggles a paused flag; when paused the rotation angles and light time stop advancing but rendering continues so the screen stays drawn (and HUD shows "PAUSED").

7. FPS: measure with performance.now(); keep a counter of frames in the last 500 ms window and update the HUD text "FPS: N" about twice per second; also show W/P state ("Wireframe: on/off", "PAUSED").

8. Main loop: requestAnimationFrame with delta time clamped to 0.05 s. Angles: ax += 0.7*dt, ay += 1.0*dt, az += 0.4*dt (rad). Handle window resize: set canvas width/height to window.innerWidth/innerHeight (use devicePixelRatio optional), recreate ImageData on size change, recompute projection center/focal.

9. Keyboard: keydown listener for 'w'/'W' toggles wireframe, 'p'/'P' toggles pause; ignore auto-repeat.

10. Code style: camelCase for functions and variables, comments in English, no external resources, no console errors. The final file must be fully functional: open in a browser and it shows a rotating, Gouraud-shaded cube with a moving light, W toggles wireframe, P pauses, FPS displayed."}
